caption: The drawing displays five distinct fireplace tools arranged side by side. From left to right, the first object is a shovel with a long, thin handle and a flat, slightly arched scoop at the end; the handle has a bulbous, ornate knob at the top. The second object is a pair of tongs featuring an identical handle design, with two elongated arms ending in pointed tips. The third object shows a poker, also featuring a matching ornate handle with a round, decorative disc just above the working end, which is a straight, narrow rod. Fourth is a rod with an even thinner shaft and a simpler, smaller knob at the top. The fifth object is another rod, which also has a decorative knob at the top, a thickened grip area, and a bent, flattened end, resembling a small hoe or scraper. The coloring in the drawing is limited to shades of gold, brass, and gray, with the metal parts rendered in a yellowish metallic color and the shafts typically in a darker gray or black, producing a realistic metallic effect. The composition is on a plain, cream-toned background with each object spaced evenly. There is also a small scale for reference at the bottom center, marked “0,” “1’,” “2’,” “3’,” and the name “HANS KORSCH” written in the lower left corner.
title: Fire Tools
